title: Responsible AI

header.html: Describe considerations for fairness in an AI solution; Describe considerations for reliability and safety in an AI solution; Describe considerations for privacy and security in an AI solution; Describe considerations for inclusiveness in an AI solution; Describe considerations for transparency in an AI solution; Describe considerations for accountability in an AI solution
the official AI-901 study guide, skills measured as of April 15, 2026

html:
1The six principles

Microsoft's approach to responsible AI is built on six principles. Each question on this topic gives a situation and asks which principle it touches.

Principle Microsoft's one-line statement The question it answers
Fairness AI systems should treat all people fairly Does the system treat similar people in similar ways?
Reliability and safety AI systems should perform reliably and safely Does it work as intended, and can it cause harm?
Privacy and security AI systems should be secure and respect privacy Is personal data protected and used with permission?
Inclusiveness AI systems should empower everyone and engage all people, regardless of their backgrounds Can everyone use it, including people with disabilities?
Transparency AI systems should be understandable Do people know how it works, what it can and cannot do?
Accountability People should be accountable for AI systems Who is responsible, and who can step in?

Exam tip

. Remember the first letters: Fairness, Reliability and safety, Privacy and security, Inclusiveness, Transparency, Accountability. Match the problem in the scenario to the principle.

2Fairness

Fairness means the system should not favor or disadvantage groups of people without a good reason.

  • Typical risk: a model trained on biased or unbalanced data gives worse results for some groups, for example a loan or hiring model that learned a historical bias.
  • Considerations: use representative training data, test results for different groups, and review the model for bias before and after release.
  • Clue words: "different results for different groups", "bias", "treats applicants unequally".
Exam tip

. Match the problem in the scenario to the principle: unequal results for groups is fairness; wrong or harmful output is reliability and safety.

3Reliability and safety

Reliability and safety means the system should work as designed, handle unexpected conditions and not cause harm.

  • Typical risk: a system gives wrong answers, fails in conditions it was not tested for, or produces harmful content.
  • Considerations: rigorous testing, handling of errors and unusual inputs, monitoring after release, and a way to turn the system off or fall back to a person. For generative AI, also filtering harmful output and checking for made-up answers (called hallucinations).
  • Clue words: "must work in all conditions", "could harm someone if wrong", "testing", "safety".

4Privacy and security

Privacy and security means the system should protect data and respect people's privacy.

  • Typical risk: training or using personal data without permission, leaking data in outputs, or letting attackers reach the system.
  • Considerations: collect only what is needed, get consent, secure stored and transmitted data, control access, and follow data-protection rules.
  • Clue words: "personal information", "consent", "data leaks", "protect customer data".

5Inclusiveness

Inclusiveness means the system should empower and engage everyone, including people with disabilities, different languages or different backgrounds.

  • Typical risk: a solution built only for a narrow group, such as a voice assistant that fails on some accents or an app that cannot be used with a screen reader.
  • Considerations: design with people of different abilities and backgrounds, offer alternatives (captions, speech, text), and test with diverse users.
  • Clue words: "accessible", "people with disabilities", "different languages and accents", "everyone can use it".
Exam tip

. Do not mix up transparency (the system is understandable) with accountability (people are responsible for it).

6Transparency

Transparency means people should understand how the system works and what its limits are.

  • Typical risk: users do not know they are talking to an AI, or cannot tell why a decision was made.
  • Considerations: tell users when AI is used, explain what the system can and cannot do, document how it was built and tested, and where possible give reasons for results.
  • Clue words: "explain how the decision was made", "users should know it is AI", "documentation".

7Accountability

Accountability means people stay responsible for AI systems and their effects.

  • Typical risk: nobody owns the outcome, or decisions are left entirely to the machine.
  • Considerations: human oversight, clear roles and responsibility, governance and review processes, and a way to audit and correct the system.
  • Clue words: "who is responsible", "human review", "governance", "oversight".

8Responsible AI for generative AI

Generative AI adds risks that fit the same principles:

Risk Principle it touches Example response
Made-up facts (hallucinations) Reliability and safety Ground answers in trusted data; ask people to check
Harmful or offensive output Reliability and safety Content filters and safety settings in the platform
Revealing private data Privacy and security Do not put secrets or personal data in prompts; control access
Biased wording or images Fairness Test with varied prompts and review outputs
Users unaware text is AI-written Transparency Label AI-generated content
No human check on important output Accountability Keep a person in the loop

Microsoft Foundry offers safety and guardrail settings that help with filtering harmful content. [Verify live] for current names and options. Beyond the study guide

9Exam Q&A

9.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors discovers that its résumé-screening model rejects applicants from one region more often. Which principle is mainly affected?

  • ATransparency
  • BInclusiveness
  • CFairness
  • DAccountability
Show the answer

Answer: C. Different results for different groups of applicants is a fairness concern.

S2A voice assistant fails to understand people with some accents or speech differences. Which principle is mainly affected?

  • APrivacy and security
  • BInclusiveness
  • CAccountability
  • DReliability and safety
Show the answer

Answer: B. Inclusiveness asks that the system works for everyone, regardless of background or ability.

S3A company tells users that an answer was written by AI and publishes what the system can and cannot do. Which principle does this support?

  • AFairness
  • BPrivacy and security
  • CTransparency
  • DReliability and safety
Show the answer

Answer: C. Being open about the use and limits of AI supports transparency.

S4A team makes sure a named manager reviews high-impact AI decisions and can overrule them. Which principle does this support?

  • AInclusiveness
  • BAccountability
  • CFairness
  • DTransparency
Show the answer

Answer: B. People stay responsible and in control: that is accountability.

S5A chatbot sometimes states false facts with confidence, and testers add checks before release. Which principle is mainly affected?

  • AInclusiveness
  • BPrivacy and security
  • CFairness
  • DReliability and safety
Show the answer

Answer: D. A system that gives wrong or harmful output is a reliability and safety concern.

S6An engineer pastes customer names and addresses into a public tool to test a prompt. Which principle is mainly at risk?

  • ATransparency
  • BInclusiveness
  • CPrivacy and security
  • DAccountability
Show the answer

Answer: C. Putting personal data where it should not go is a privacy and security risk.

9.2 Recall questions

R1Name the six responsible AI principles.

Show the answer

Fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability.

R2Which principle says people should be accountable for AI systems?

Show the answer

Accountability.

R3Which principle covers people with disabilities being able to use a system?

Show the answer

Inclusiveness.

R4What is a hallucination?

Show the answer

A confident answer from a generative model that is made up or wrong.

R5Which principle says AI systems should be understandable?

Show the answer

Transparency.

R6Biased training data is mainly a problem for which principle?

Show the answer

Fairness.

10Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Fairness treat people fairly; watch biased data; test for different groups
Reliability and safety work as designed, handle surprises, no harm; testing, monitoring, filters
Privacy and security protect data, consent, least data, access control
Inclusiveness everyone can use it: disabilities, languages, accents
Transparency understandable: say it is AI, explain limits and reasons
Accountability people stay responsible: oversight, governance, audit
